1. Jaime is imaginative (given).
2. Imaginative ⇒ (makes-music XOR dances-well). So Jaime must do exactly one of making music or dancing well.

Case A: Jaime makes music (and does not dance well).
   a) She does not write poems (given).
   b) Premise: (makes-music XOR writes-poems) ⇒ loves-art. Since she makes music and not writes poems, she satisfies the antecedent; therefore Jaime loves art.

   d) Premise: values-comfort ⇒ (NOT-creative XOR entrepreneurial). Jaime is not entrepreneurial (given), so to satisfy the XOR she must be creative (and not entrepreneurial). Hence in this case Jaime is creative.

Case B: Jaime dances well (and does not make music).
   a) Premise: dances-well ⇒ (has-rhythm AND can-express-emotions). That would require Jaime to be able to express emotions, but it is given she cannot express emotions. Contradiction. So Case B fails.

Only Case A survives, and in it we derived that Jaime is creative. Therefore the context uniquely entails she is creative.
